sub_answers.sub_question: What documented instances of participant shortages, event cancellations, or category omissions have occurred at Latvian championships?
sub_answers.text: The Riga Football Cup was held intermittently between 1910 and 1936, indicating interruptions in the competition's continuity. [d17125690s1p0] The Riga Football Cup was replaced by the Latvian Football Cup in 1937, showing a categorical transition of national cup competitions. [d17125690s1p0] The Latvian Football Union organized a Latvian Championship between 1922 and 1927, after which Virsliga replaced the Latvian Championship in 1927. [d17125690s1p0]

sub_answers.sub_question: What governance disputes or controversies (selection, judging, federation decisions) have been reported in Latvian figure skating history?
How have resource limitations (rinks, funding, coaching availability) impacted staging or competitiveness of Latvian national championships?
sub_answers.text: Latvia had been one of very few Baltic footballing nations without a primary national stadium for many years, reflecting a resource limitation affecting national football staging. [d17125690s7p0] The national team played most international games in Daugava Stadium and Skonto Stadium, and neither stadium met UEFA/FIFA standards due to low seating capacity of less than 11,000. [d17125690s7p0] A planned modern stadium project was put on hold due to unclear funding strategies among the UAE investors, the Latvian football governing body, and other organizations. [d17125690s7p0]

sub_answers.sub_question: Have there been criticisms or external assessments about the competitiveness or international relevance of Latvia's national championships?
sub_answers.text: Daugava Stadium and Skonto Stadium do not meet UEFA/FIFA standards because their seating capacity is less than 11,000, which limits their international relevance. [d17125690s7p0] The Latvian Football Federation partnered with an investor and envisioned a 15,000- to 20,000-seat stadium to attract international events, indicating concerns about current facilities' competitiveness on the international stage. [d17125690s7p0]
